what_it_does: When you send personal data to an online service for processing — say, for medical analysis or financial advice — you have no way to technically verify that the server does not secretly copy or leak it, because the code runs entirely on hardware you do not control. Pave addresses this by running the processing program inside a secure walled-off area on the server called a sandbox (built on Intel SGX, a hardware feature that creates a cryptographically isolated compartment that even the server's owner cannot inspect). A monitor sitting at the boundary of the sandbox tracks every piece of data entering and leaving, and blocks any flow that would expose your private information to unauthorized parties. You can verify remotely that this setup is genuinely in place before sending your data, because SGX hardware can produce a signed proof (called remote attestation) of exactly what code is running and that the sandbox is intact.
